previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and hypercholesterolemia was admitted for left-sided chest pain radiating to the arm and leg, which woke her at 3 a.m. The pain was similar to prior episodes previously determined to be non-cardiac. Serial troponins were negative, EKGs showed no changes, and a chest X-ray revealed no acute abnormalities, ruling out acute cardiac or pulmonary causes. Her symptoms were attributed to likely musculoskeletal, neuropathic, or gastrointestinal origins. She presented with hyperglycemia (blood glucose 500), managed by adjusting her insulin regimen to 60 units glargine at bedtime and 20 units lispro with meals, plus sliding scale. She was restarted on omeprazole after clarification that her insurance covers it and advised to resume daily aspirin. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged and clear instructions for medication adjustments, blood sugar monitoring, and when to seek care.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ female with fall and head trauma 8 days ago, now with
head pain and complaints of visual changes.

COMPARISON:  CT head from ___ and ___ as well as MRI of the brain on
___.

NON-CONTRAST HEAD CT:  There is no evidence of acute intracranial hemorrhage,
edema, mass effect, shift of normally midline structures, effacement of the
basal cisterns, hydrocephalus, or of large vascular territory infarction.
Subcortical white matter hypodensities are again likely due to chronic small
vessel ischemic disease and is unchanged from multiple prior studies,
particularly along the right corona radiata.  Hypodensities along the external
capsule bilaterally and also in the basal ganglia likely represent chronic
lacunar infarcts.  Vascular calcifications are noted along the cavernous
carotid arteries and the vertebral arteries.  The soft tissues and orbits
appear intact.  No acute fracture is noted within the visualized calvarium.
Rounded region of relative lucency measuring approximately 1.6 cm in the left
frontal region is unchanged from multiple prior studies dating back to ___
and likely represents a benign entity.  The visualized paranasal sinuses and
mastoid air cells remain well aerated.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of acute intracranial process. MRI is a more
sensitive examination for the detection of acute ischemia.
